3. Clearly note the date and time of the inspection as well as the vehicle's VIN (Vehicle Identification Number), make, model, and year.
4. Conduct the brake test following standard safety protocols and test procedures, including an inspection of the brake system's components (e.g., pads, rotors, calipers, fluid levels, and lines).
5. Identify the equipment and methods used to conduct the brake test(s) (e.g., brake dynamometer, brake pedal feel test, visual inspection).
